Talavishiraaj Groups (“we”, “us”, “our”) is committed to protecting your personal information and your right to privacy. This Privacy Policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, how we protect it, and what rights you have under applicable laws, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (“DPDP Act”).
By using our website, Systems products (including Prism), or engaging with us as a client or partner, you agree that your personal data will be handled as described in this Policy.
1. Who We Are and Scope
This Policy applies to:
Visitors to our websites (including tjgroups.com and talavishiraajgroups.com).
Prospective and existing clients, partners, and suppliers.
Users of our systems‑oriented services and products, including Prism.

Talavishiraaj Groups operates as a remote‑first organisation based in India and serving clients globally. For most website and marketing activities we act as a “Data Fiduciary” under the DPDP Act and as a “data controller” under other data protection laws where applicable. When we process personal data on behalf of our clients (for example, through Systems or Prism), we act as a “Data Processor” under the relevant Data Processing Agreement (DPA) or similar terms.
You can contact us at:
info@talavishiraajgroups.com.
2. Information We Collect
We collect personal information in the following situations.
2.1. Information you provide directly
When you interact with us, you may provide:
Name
Email address
Phone number
Company name and role
Project, inquiry, or diagnostic details
Billing and invoicing details (for paying clients)
This includes data submitted through contact forms, demo requests, consultations, Systems/Prism onboarding forms, and direct email or messaging channels.
2.2. Usage and device data
When you visit our websites or use our products, our servers may automatically log:
IP address and approximate location
Browser type and version
Device identifiers and operating system
Pages viewed, time spent, and navigation paths
This information is collected through server logs and basic analytics at the infrastructure level, not through third‑party tracking pixels or marketing cookies.
2.3. Project and diagnostic data
When you engage us for work or use our products, we may process:
Project‑related information and datasets you share
Configuration details, prompts, parameters, and files you upload
Outputs and reports generated by Prism or other Systems products

This data may include personal data of your customers, employees, or partners, depending on how you choose to use our services. In those cases we process personal data as your Data Processor under a separate DPA or similar terms.
3. How We Use Your Information
We use your information for the following purposes:
To provide, operate, and improve our services and products, including Systems and Prism.
To respond to your inquiries, proposals, and support requests.
To configure, implement, and maintain solutions for you as a client.
To send you service‑related communications, updates, and security notices.
To analyse usage and improve performance, reliability, and user experience.
To maintain the security of our systems, prevent abuse, and detect fraud.
To comply with legal obligations and respond to lawful requests from authorities.
We may also use anonymised or aggregated data derived from project and diagnostic data to:
Improve our models, systems, and internal research.
Develop benchmarks and insights that do not identify any individual or client.
We do not sell your personal data.
4. Legal Bases and Consent
Where required by law, we rely on one or more of the following legal bases to process your personal data:
Your consent (e.g., for certain marketing communications).
Performance of a contract with you or your organisation (e.g., to deliver a project or diagnostic engagement).
Our legitimate interests in operating, securing, and improving our business, provided these are not overridden by your rights.
Compliance with legal obligations or to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.
You can withdraw consent for marketing at any time by using an unsubscribe link or contacting us at
info@talavishiraajgroups.com.
5. Sharing of Data
We may share your information with:
Service providers and sub‑processors who support our operations (for example, cloud hosting, AI model providers, infrastructure analytics, payment processors, email delivery services).
Partners and subcontractors who help us deliver specific projects, subject to appropriate confidentiality and data protection obligations.
Professional advisers (such as auditors and lawyers) where reasonably necessary.
Legal authorities when required by law or to protect our rights, users, or the public.
We share only the minimum information needed and require our service providers and partners to process personal data in line with this Policy and applicable data protection laws.
6. International Transfers
Because we work with clients and service providers globally, your personal data may be transferred to and processed in countries other than your own, which may have different data protection laws.
Where we transfer personal data across borders, we implement appropriate safeguards as required by the DPDP Act and other applicable laws, such as contractual protections and security measures.
7. Cookies and Similar Technologies

Nothing is set while you read the site. Two things can change that, and both require you to accept the notice shown on your first visit. Neither is loaded, and no request is made to either provider, unless you do.

The first is Microsoft Clarity, which we use to understand how the site is used: which pages hold attention, how far people read, where they go next and where they give up. It records page interactions and may replay a session to show us where a page confused someone. It sets its own cookies. Text you type into form fields is masked by default and we keep that setting on, so the content of an enquiry is not captured by it.
The second is Cal.com, which provides the booking calendar inside our page if you choose to book a call. It may set its own cookies under its own terms to run the booking.

We use no advertising pixels, no remarketing tags and no social network trackers, and we do not sell or share this information. Separately from any of the above, our hosting provider records ordinary request information as described in Section 2.2 for security and reliability, and our page view counting is cookieless.

You can decline, and declining costs you nothing: the contact form reaches us the same way. Your choice is remembered in your browser so you are not asked again, and clearing your site data resets it. If we introduce anything beyond the two named above, we will update this Policy and ask before enabling it.
8. Data Retention
We retain personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes described in this Policy, including:
providing services and maintaining business records;
complying with legal, accounting, or reporting requirements;
resolving disputes and enforcing our agreements.
When data is no longer needed, we will delete or anonymise it in line with our internal policies and applicable law. You may also request deletion of your personal data (see Section 9).
9. Your Rights and Choices
Under the DPDP Act and other applicable laws, you may have the right to:
Request access to the personal data we hold about you.
Request corrections to inaccurate or incomplete data.
Request deletion of your personal data, subject to legal limitations.
Withdraw consent to processing where we rely on consent.
Request a copy of your personal data in a portable format, where feasible.
To exercise these rights, please contact us at
info@talavishiraajgroups.com with sufficient details to identify you and your request. We may need to verify your identity before acting on your request.
10. Grievance and Data Protection Contact
We take privacy‑related concerns seriously. If you have a concern or grievance about how we handle your personal data, you can contact our Grievance Officer / Data Protection Lead at:
info@talavishiraajgroups.com
We will aim to acknowledge and address your grievance within timelines required by the DPDP Act and applicable rules.
11. Security
We use reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect your personal data from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, or access.
No system is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security. However, we regularly review and improve our security controls and practices.
12. Children’s Privacy

Our services and website are not directed to children under the age of 18, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from children. If you believe that a child has provided us with personal data, please contact us and we will take appropriate steps.
13. Changes to This Policy
We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in law, technology, or our business practices. We will post the updated version on this page with a new “Last Updated” date.

If changes are material, we may notify you through additional means (for example, by email or a site notice) where appropriate. Continued use of our website or services after changes take effect means you accept the updated terms.
14. Contact
If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or our data practices, please contact us at:
info@talavishiraajgroups.com

This Refund Policy describes how Talavishiraaj Groups handles refunds for consulting, systems‑oriented services, and productised offerings such as Prism. It applies to engagements unless a separate signed agreement (such as a Statement of Work or Master Services Agreement) specifies a different refund structure, in which case the signed agreement will prevail.

We invest significant time in consultant allocation, research preparation, systems configuration, and delivery planning for every engagement. Our refund approach is designed to balance fairness to clients with the operational realities of high‑involvement services.
1. Consultation Engagements
Consultation‑based engagements include structured advisory sessions, assessment readouts, and strategy consultations.
Once a consultation session is scheduled and confirmed, the fee is non‑refundable.
Sessions may be rescheduled once with at least 48 hours’ prior written notice, subject to consultant availability.
Reschedule requests made with less than 48 hours’ notice may be treated as completed sessions and may not be eligible for rescheduling or refund.
2. Service and Implementation Engagements

For multi‑phase service and implementation projects, including systems design, research, architecture, and execution, refunds (where considered) are based on the project stage and work completed at the time of the request.
Project Stage | Refund Eligibility (up to) |
Before project assembly / kickoff | 90% of fees paid |
Discovery / onboarding initiated | 75% of fees paid |
Research & assessment phase active | 60% of fees paid |
Strategy / blueprint development active | 40% of fees paid |
Implementation / execution initiated | Case‑by‑case review |
Project substantially completed | Non‑refundable |
Refund calculations may account for:
Consultant allocation and research preparation time.
Discovery and planning work already performed.
Documented deliverables and work products completed to date.
Administrative overhead and scheduling commitments.
Payment gateway, banking, and international reconciliation costs.
Where a signed SOW or contract defines different percentages or milestones, those terms will apply.
3. Systems and Prism (Upfront Payments)
Systems and Prism are structured, systems‑driven offerings that typically require upfront payment before any analysis or configuration begins.
Unless stated otherwise in the applicable Order Form or SOW:
a) Before any work or data collection begins

If you request a refund before we collect any client information for the engagement and before configuration or onboarding work has started, a refund of up to 80% of fees paid may be considered on written request. This reflects initial scheduling, planning, and administrative effort already committed.
b) After work has started and information has been collected

Once onboarding, diagnostic data collection, research, assessment, or configuration work has started, any refund request will be evaluated based on the project stage and completed work, using the same stage‑based structure defined in Section 2 (“Service and Implementation Engagements”).

In such cases, we may consider a partial refund aligned to the documented stage (for example, Discovery/Onboarding, Research & Assessment, Strategy/Blueprint, or Implementation), taking into account the work already delivered, internal resources allocated, and costs incurred.
c) After diagnostic outputs or reports are delivered
After Prism or Systems outputs/reports have been delivered, fees are non‑refundable, as the core value of these offerings lies in the expertise, analysis, and deliverables already provided.
Any specific refund rules or exceptions for Systems or Prism agreed in your signed contract will override this general policy.
4. How to Request a Refund
To request a refund or raise a concern:
Send a written request to info@talavishiraajgroups.com with:
Engagement name and reference.
Invoice number(s).
Reason for the request.
Any supporting documentation.
We will review your request against:
The project stage and work completed.
The signed contract / SOW and this Refund Policy.
Any supporting documentation and communication history.

We generally aim to respond with an initial decision or clarification request within a reasonable business timeframe and to process any approved refund within a reasonable period after confirmation, subject to bank and payment‑gateway timelines.
5. Payment Channels and Processing
Global payments are processed through approved international payment processors and banking partners. Refunds, where approved, are:
Issued only to the original payment method used for the transaction, and
Processed in the original billing currency, subject to exchange rates, bank charges, and international reconciliation timelines.

Due to currency conversion and fluctuating foreign exchange rates, the amount you receive back in your local currency may differ from the amount originally paid. Talavishiraaj Groups is not responsible for any foreign exchange losses, currency conversion differences, bank spreads, or international transaction/processing fees charged by your bank, card issuer, or payment provider in connection with the original payment or any refund.
We are not responsible for delays caused by banks, intermediaries, or payment‑gateway providers once the refund has been initiated from our side.
6. Disputes and Escalation
If you disagree with a refund decision or have concerns about how your request was handled, you may escalate in writing via our official contact channel:
info@talavishiraajgroups.com
We will provide a structured review based on:
The engagement documentation (proposal, SOW, MSA).
Delivery‑stage evidence and internal logs.
This Refund Policy and any applicable consumer or contract law.
Nothing in this Refund Policy is intended to limit any non‑waivable statutory rights you may have under applicable consumer protection laws.
7. Data Protection and Refunds

Refunds relate only to commercial fees and do not affect our obligations to protect any personal data or confidential information processed during an engagement. Once client information has been collected for Systems, Prism, or any other service, we will continue to handle that data in accordance with:

any applicable Data Processing Agreement (DPA) or confidentiality agreement with you, and
the requirements of the DPDP Act and other applicable data protection laws.

Depending on the circumstances, we may be required to retain certain records for legal, audit, or compliance purposes even after a refund is processed or an engagement ends. Where retention is no longer necessary, we will delete or anonymise personal data in line with our internal data‑retention policies.

We may revise this Refund Policy from time to time to reflect changes in our services, payment infrastructure, or legal requirements. The updated version will be posted on this page with a new “Last Updated” date. Continued use of our services after changes take effect means you accept the updated terms.

Talavishiraaj Groups is committed to professional, timely, and structured delivery of all workflow intelligence and implementation services. Our delivery framework is designed to ensure transparency, quality, and measurable outcomes at every engagement stage.

This Delivery Policy provides general guidance and works together with the specific terms, Statement(s) of Work, and Master Services Agreement for each engagement. If there is any conflict, the signed agreement will take precedence for that engagement.
Delivery Timelines
Delivery timelines vary by engagement type and are subject to the following general parameters:
Decision Engagements (including Prism): Typically completed within 10 to 13 business days from confirmed intake and completion of the required client information forms.
Implementation Engagements: Project‑specific timelines are defined in the initial Strategic Roadmap and communicated clearly at engagement initiation.
Consultation Sessions: Scheduled within agreed availability windows; timing is subject to mutual scheduling confirmation.
Stakeholder Dependencies: All timelines are subject to stakeholder responsiveness and the timely sharing of required organisational information, access, and approvals.
Timelines communicated at the start of an engagement are planning estimates and may be adjusted by mutual agreement based on updated scope, dependencies, and priorities.
Client Responsibilities
Successful, timely delivery is a collaborative effort. Clients are expected to support the engagement through:
Timely sharing of required organisational information and relevant data.
Stakeholder availability for structured sessions and feedback rounds.
Prompt communication, clarifications, and approval turnarounds.
Coordination support during active implementation phases.
Designation of a primary point of contact for engagement coordination.

Delays arising from insufficient client responsiveness, unavailability of required information, or third‑party constraints may extend the delivery timeline accordingly. Such delays and dependency‑driven shifts do not constitute a delivery failure or breach of commitment by Talavishiraaj Groups.
Scope Clarification
Delivery scope is defined at engagement initiation and governed by the agreed engagement parameters. The following clarifications apply to all engagements:

Decision vs. Implementation Scope: Decision engagements, including Prism and other Systems diagnostics, produce visibility, recommendations, and a structured roadmap. They do not include direct implementation unless a separate implementation engagement is initiated.

Excluded Items: Items not explicitly included in the engagement scope, proposal, or Statement of Work are excluded from delivery. Scope extensions or changes require a separate agreement and may impact timelines and fees.
Dependency Limitations: Deliverables dependent on third‑party systems, client data, or external approvals are subject to those dependencies and may affect the delivery timeline and approach.

Engagement Assumptions: All engagements operate on the assumption that provided information is accurate and complete. Material inaccuracies or omissions may require scope reassessment and timeline revision.
Communication Structure
Professional, structured communication is central to our delivery process:
Scheduling: All sessions are scheduled through agreed communication channels with sufficient notice provided to both parties.
Timezone Flexibility: We accommodate cross‑timezone engagements and agree on scheduling windows at the outset of each engagement.
Communication Channels: Primary communication is conducted through agreed digital channels. All material decisions, approvals, and confirmations are documented in writing.
Progress Updates: For longer engagements, structured progress updates are provided at agreed intervals to maintain alignment and clarity.
Standard Deliverables
For decision engagements, delivery typically includes a structured package containing:
Comprehensive report and strategy documentation (digital format, such as PDF).
Recorded clarity or review session (secure video delivery where applicable).
Visual workflow and systems maps.
Actionable implementation roadmap.
Supporting documentation and reference assets as relevant.
Implementation engagement deliverables are project‑specific and defined within the engagement roadmap, proposal, and/or Statement of Work.
Data Protection and Confidentiality

Any client information and data processed as part of decision or implementation engagements is handled in accordance with our Privacy Policy, applicable Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) or NDAs, and relevant data protection laws, including the DPDP Act where applicable.
Outcome Disclaimer

While we strive to deliver high‑quality analysis, strategies, and implementations, all engagements are provided on a professional best‑effort basis. Delivery of services, recommendations, or roadmaps does not by itself guarantee specific business outcomes such as revenue growth, lead volume, or other performance metrics, unless expressly agreed in a separate signed contract.
For information on fees, cancellations, and partial refunds, please refer to our Refund Policy.

A structured, enterprise‑grade governance framework governing risk identification, delivery quality assurance, and recovery protocols across all engagements. This framework operates alongside the specific contractual terms (including any Master Services Agreement, Statement of Work, NDA, and Data Processing Agreement) governing each client engagement.
Governance Commitment

At Talavishiraaj Groups, governance is a foundational element of every engagement, not an afterthought. Our Risk & Mitigation Framework ensures that every engagement is protected by proactive risk identification, structured quality standards, and clear recovery protocols.

This framework operates together with our Refund Policy, Delivery Policy, Privacy Policy, and Confidentiality & Data Handling commitments as part of a comprehensive governance architecture and is designed to support compliance with applicable data protection and professional standards.
Risk Framework Categories
Delivery & Execution Risks
Identifying and addressing workflow bottlenecks, coordination gaps, and execution misalignments before they impact delivery quality or timeline.
Workflow Visibility AssessmentExecution Alignment ReviewCoordination Framework Design
Technology & Systems Risks
Ensuring systems integrity, data security, and infrastructure scalability for AI, automation, and technology implementation.
Systems Integrity ReviewScalability AssessmentData Governance Framework
Strategic & Organisational Risks
Aligning systems implementation with long‑term organisational goals, execution readiness, and strategic maturity.
Strategic Alignment ReviewExecution Readiness AssessmentOrganisational Maturity Mapping
Delivery Recovery & Quality Escalation Framework
An internal delivery quality review may be initiated under the following conditions:
Expression of delivery dissatisfaction by the client.
Communication breakdown or responsiveness concerns.
Unclear or insufficiently structured recommendations.
Missed delivery timelines attributable to internal factors.
Systems misalignment or implementation confusion.
Delivery quality concerns raised formally in writing.
Internal Review Categories
Clarity Quality
Were recommendations structured, actionable, and clearly understandable for the intended audience and organisational context?
Systems Accuracy
Were the core workflow bottlenecks, systems gaps, and coordination friction points correctly identified and substantiated?
Strategic Relevance
Did recommendations align with execution readiness, scalability stage, and organisational maturity at the time of engagement?
Delivery Professionalism
Were communication standards, timeline commitments, presentation quality, and stakeholder engagement maintained throughout?
Actionability
Could the recommendations realistically be implemented with the organisational resources and capability available?
Recovery Actions
Depending on the outcome of an internal delivery review, recovery actions may include:
Structured clarification sessions.
Roadmap refinement and supplemental documentation.
Supplemental consultation session.
Delivery adjustments and scope reassessment.
Structured internal quality review.
Partial service credit where appropriate and applicable.

Nothing is set in your browser until you answer the banner, and declining keeps it that way. Accepting permits two things and no more: measuring how the site is used, and loading a booking calendar if you go to book a call.

That is a short enough list to set out precisely, so the whole position is below rather than buried in a policy. Everything on this page describes what the site does today, and it was checked in a browser rather than copied from a template.
What this site does and does not do
Cookies set by this site itselfNone.
This domain sets no cookies of its own, for any purpose. The cookies that can appear if you accept belong to the two third parties named below and are set under their own terms.
Data stored in your browser by usYour answer, and nothing else.

One entry holding one word, recording whether you accepted or declined, so you are not asked again. Nothing else is written to local storage or session storage. Clear site data and it goes, along with the record of your answer.
Advertising and cross site trackingNone.
There are no advertising pixels, no remarketing tags and no social network trackers anywhere on the site.
Page view countingCookieless.
Vercel Analytics counts page views without cookies and without building a profile of you. It cannot follow you to other websites and it runs whether or not you accept anything.
Behaviour analyticsOnly if you allow it.

If you accept, Microsoft Clarity shows us which pages hold attention, how far people read, where they go next and where they give up. It sets cookies and can replay a session. Text you type into forms is masked and stays masked. Decline and it is never loaded.
FontsSelf hosted.
Typefaces are served from this domain rather than from a font network, so loading a page does not announce your visit to a third party.
Server logsStandard.
Our hosting provider records ordinary request information such as IP address and user agent, for security and reliability. That is described in the privacy policy.
The third parties, and when they load

Two, and both wait for your answer. Microsoft Clarity measures how the site is used, and loads only if you accept. Cal.com provides the booking calendar inside our page, and loads only if you accept and then go to book. Decline and no request reaches either of them, ever: the scripts are not inserted rather than inserted and idle.

Both set their own cookies under their own terms once loaded. We do not control those and we do not read them. Declining costs you nothing that matters: the contact form reaches us identically and involves nobody else.
What the banner is actually asking

Two things, and they are worth separating. The first is measurement: whether we may see which pages held your attention, how far you read and where you gave up, so the site can be made less annoying than it is. The second is the booking calendar, which runs inside our page and belongs to Cal.com. Decline and neither loads. You can read every page, and the contact form reaches us just as well.

There is an irony in it worth stating rather than hiding. A banner you can dismiss has to remember that you dismissed it, so your answer is the one thing this site does write to your browser. It is a single entry holding a single word, it is readable only by this site, and remembering a consent decision is permitted without asking permission for it. If you clear site data it comes back, because the record of your answer went with it.
Neither answer is made easier than the other, and declining is not a dead end anywhere on the site.
The privacy policy sets out what we collect when you contact us, how long it is kept and your rights over it.
